en: The Sutra on the Dhāraṇī of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Censor of the Third Order, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fata, by Imperial Decree.
I take refuge in the Universal Dharmakāya, the light of the Perfectly Awakened One—the cause of purity and equality throughout the three times, pervading the entire realm of space;
In the emanated bodies that bring benefit and happiness to humans and devas, manifesting while dwelling in the sovereign state of the ten stages;
Who practice great generosity and make vows to deliver all sentient beings.
Adorned with the marks of merit, he is named Samantabhadra; now he shall proclaim the secret teaching of mantras.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, desiring to manifest vast transformations, entered into samādhi.
He is named Mahesvara of the Three Realms.
Having entered this samādhi,
from the realm of pure space, he...
Manifesting countless bodies like grains of dust and sand,
they pervade all worlds throughout the great trichiliocosm.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas residing in all the Buddha-fields—
He extended his right hand and stroked the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, praising him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Buddha!
You should now proclaim the supreme dhāraṇī method, the Mother of all Buddhas."
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva emitted a thousand rays of light from his body, which universally illuminated the ten directions;
all buddha-fields were shaken throughout.
He then spoke the dhāraṇī:
*Tadyathā | oṃ namo narmasatvabuddhānīśvaramahābuddhāya asamasama*.
Om amṛta samānanda sama-gagana-samatrpya-vaśa-sama-viśa-sama-paramārtha-sama-svabhāva-samatathāgata-samārjava-sa.
Maṃśuti samabuddha-samadharma-tathāgata-samasaṃgha-viśama-sama-ekana-ya-sāgara-viśuddha-loka-hihi-ra-buddha-ra-buddha-vijaya-vi.
Jaya aṃ praśāktānāṃ naya na ya haṃ jīrḍiṣṭāna svabhāga aṃ saṃlāyaṃ lāya dharma-āgrādha dhara dhara jaya jaya hūṃ.
HŪṂ DHAMA DHAMA SVĀHĀ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra,
having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
The Buddha then observed that the body of that bodhisattva was a transformation body manifested by a former buddha of the past out of compassion for all sentient beings.
Pervading all the worlds within the three realms,
at that time, the great bodhisattvas,
as well as devas, humans, asuras, and others, [were present].
Emerging from all vajra peaks,
they depart from their own seats of great magnificence adorned with gold and jewels,
come before the Bodhisattva, and speak these words themselves:
Homage to the Great Dharani Method for Attaining Supreme Buddhahood, which is the ocean of boundless great merit of Great Compassion and Great Benevolence,
and which is well able to benefit the countless sentient beings of the three realms throughout the past, future, and present.
It causes one to dwell securely in the station of the Great Dharma.
The Buddha said: "If a person hears this great *dhāraṇī* method, all the sins committed throughout boundless eons shall be entirely extinguished."
It can also dry up the great ocean of afflictions and destroy the high mountain of the view of self,
just as if a person were to see hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
Even the roots of goodness cultivated throughout boundless eons cannot equal the merit of this mantra.
This great dhāraṇī is the ocean of the perfect and great merit of the heart of all Tathāgatas.
Yet it is able to give birth to the seeds of bodhi-wisdom and accomplish the stage of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā-bhūmi),
such that none of the Buddha-dharmas can equal it.
The name of this great dhāraṇī is difficult to hear even in hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of kalpas.
If there is anyone who, regarding this sūtra—
Those sentient beings who uphold, recite, and reverently make offerings to it will skillfully understand the dhāraṇī;
they shall sustain their life of wisdom and abide in the state of a Tathāgata.
One accomplishes all merits. If there is anyone who reads and recites this sutra once,
twice, or even up to three times.
That person shall attain the most supreme merit;
they will be able to extinguish all sins and sever all afflictions,
and furthermore, they will encounter all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
One shall not suffer any sorrow or affliction.
If one recites this with single-minded devotion in a secluded place, such as beneath a solitary tree, [the results will be attained].
That person will attain all dharmas of accomplishment and be loved and respected by the multitude.
If there is anyone who sits cross-legged in a great forest and recites this sutra for seven full cycles, [they shall likewise achieve these results].
Before long, that person will attain great meditative concentration (*samādhi*) and sever all afflictions (*kleśa*).
Furthermore, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva will appear before them, seated in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
If a person, according to their own capacity, makes offerings of incense and flowers while reciting this dhāraṇī,
they will see the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in their dreams, even if they fall into a deep sleep.
Extending his right hand, he emitted the light of the Dharma,
which bathed and illuminated their bodies and minds, and spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent, O Son of the Buddha!"
Through the transformation of the Tathāgata’s great maṇḍala,
one attains the rank of a Great Bodhisattva,
with body and mind in peace and bliss.
Possessing great merit, virtue, and wisdom,
they shall constantly behold the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra.
If a person, with a mind of compassion...
If one reads and recites this sutra for the sake of all sentient beings,
that person will attain the fulfillment of the ten pāramitās and eliminate all afflictions, transgressions, and defilements.
Furthermore, gods and humans will provide protection, and the Tathāgata will praise them,
saying: "O Son of the Buddha, if you practice in accordance with this,
before long you shall enter the stage of Samantabhadra."
The Sutra on the Dhāraṇī of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva Spoken by the Buddha.
